title: A named conflict-of-interest waiver is written into the Atlas itself rather than granted administratively
content:
A.1.8.1.1.1 requires that the Core Council Risk Advisor "must be held by an entity without involvement in any business, political, or governance-related activities that could create a conflict of interest, either directly or indirectly." A.1.8.1.1.2 designates BA Labs. A.1.8.1.1.2.1 then reconciles the two: "BA Labs is granted a limited waiver to the requirement that the Core Council Risk Advisor must not be involved in other business activities that could result in a conflict of interest. This waiver applies only to BA Labs' work with Ethena."

The mechanism is what makes this worth recording. The waiver is not a facilitator decision, a private carve-out, or a footnote in a contract — it is a numbered Atlas Document at a specific tree position, subject to the same amendment process as any other Primary Document, and permanently visible to anyone reading the rule it modifies.

Three properties follow. It is **discoverable**: a reader of the independence requirement encounters the exception in the same subtree rather than needing to know it exists. It is **bounded**: "applies only to BA Labs' work with Ethena" — one entity, one counterparty, no general licence. And it is **revocable only through governance**, since removing it means editing the Atlas.

The generalizable pattern is that the Atlas prefers a documented exception to an unenforced rule. The alternative designs are both worse: write the independence requirement loosely enough that BA Labs complies (weakening it for every future holder), or leave the conflict unaddressed and rely on nobody noticing. Naming the exception keeps the rule strict and puts the specific compromise on the record where it can be argued about.

The cost is that constitutional text now contains a commercial particular that will go stale, and that the waiver's continuation requires no periodic re-justification — it persists silently until someone proposes removing it.
description: A.1.8.1.1.2.1 grants BA Labs a limited waiver from the Risk Advisor independence requirement, scoped explicitly to its work with Ethena — an exception that only governance can alter.
